reason: Source holds: packet.js quran 7 --verse 3.92 has the evidence words verbatim (node string match true); Abu Ja'far in his own voice glosses al-birr as God's kindness, His favour in bringing them into His Garden and turning His punishment away, then paraphrases 'until you give in alms of what you love and wish to keep for yourselves, of your choicest wealth', so both halves of the reading are his; locator right; verse.js ok (Al 'Imran 3:92, at 384); entry-check ok. What breaks is the sentence itself: the only plural antecedent it gives for 'them' in 'bringing them into His Garden' is 'those dying in disbelief' in the context clause, since the plain sense never says whom 3:92 addresses. As written, the sentence can be read as al-Tabari saying God brings those who die in disbelief into His Garden, the reverse of 3:91 and of his gloss, which names the addressees as 'O believers' (ayyuha al-mu'minun). The brief's voice asks the context clause to say to whom the ayah speaks, and it does not. Naming the believers fixes it at 44 words (gated ok in scratch/revrefute-better-d007.json).
better: After a ransom of gold is refused to those dying in disbelief, the surah turns to giving; al-Tabari, on 3:92, reads the piety as God’s kindness in bringing the believers into His Garden, reached by giving from the wealth they most wish to keep.
